The European Commission proposed adjusting the timeline for high-risk AI rules by up to 16 months so that they would start to apply once the Commission confirms needed standards and tools are available (the 'AI Omnibus'/Digital Omnibus proposal).

The Digital Package on Simplification ('AI Omnibus') legislative proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025, political agreement between Council and Parliament was reached on 7 May 2026, and the Omnibus regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026.
As amended by the AI Omnibus, the obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027.
As amended by the AI Omnibus, obligations for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products listed in Annex I apply from 2 August 2028.

Article 113 of the AI Act, as described in legal analysis, provides that Chapter III, Sections 1, 2 and 3 (except Article 6(5)) apply from 2 December 2027, consistent with the amended Annex III deadline.

One commentary describes 2 December 2027 (Annex III) and 2 August 2028 (Annex I) as 'backstop dates' negotiated in the Omnibus process, noting that if the amendments were not approved before 2 August 2026, the original high-risk provisions would technically apply from that date.

A news blog claims that under a 'final text agreed in September 2026,' the Annex III high-risk obligations deadline was moved further to 2 August 2029, citing unready harmonised standards and notified bodies.

Several commentary/news sources describe 2 August 2026 as the (then-current or still-applicable) deadline for Annex III high-risk obligations, without reference to the later Omnibus-amended 2 December 2027 date.

The EU AI Act Service Desk's guidance on Article 111 states that the Regulation applies to operators of certain pre-existing high-risk AI systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026, tying significant-change obligations to that date.

The consolidated official EU AI Act text (version dated 27.07.2026, reflecting Omnibus amendment 'M1') refers to 'the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113' rather than citing 2 August 2026 directly, for the same Article 111(2) provision on pre-existing high-risk systems.
One source describes an extended transition for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products as running to 2 August 2027, rather than 2 August 2028.
A news blog attributes the amended Annex III deadline of 2 December 2027 to a specific legal instrument, 'Regulation (EU) 2026/1744,' part of the Digital Omnibus on AI.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI System Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
As originally adopted, the EU AI Act set 2 August 2026 as the date on which obligations for high-risk AI systems under Annex III would apply (high confidence). However, following the "AI Omnibus"/Digital Omnibus simplification process, which entered into force on 27 July 2026, this deadline was postponed to **2 December 2027** for Annex III systems, with a separate date of **2 August 2028** for high-risk systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I (high confidence). Some commentary and news sources have not yet updated to reflect this change, and one unverified blog claims a further delay to 2029, creating notable confusion in the current source landscape.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (as adopted in 2024)
Under the AI Act as originally adopted, high-risk AI system obligations—including those under Annex III—were scheduled to become applicable 36 months after entry into force, on 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)).

### The Omnibus Amendment Process
The European Commission proposed adjusting the high-risk rules timeline by up to 16 months, so that obligations would begin only once the Commission confirmed that necessary standards and compliance tools were available (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). The "Digital Package on Simplification" (AI Omnibus) was formally adopted on 19 November 2025, political agreement between Council and Parliament was reached on 7 May 2026, and the amending regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) ([Shaping Europe's Digital Future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

### Current (Amended) Deadlines
As amended, obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in **Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027** (high confidence), corroborated by multiple EU guidance pages and legal-analysis sources ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [AI Omnibus Enters Into Force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force), [Timeline for Implementation](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)). Legal analysis of Article 113 confirms that Chapter III, Sections 1–3 (except Article 6(5)) apply from this date (medium confidence) ([Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). Separately, obligations for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products under **Annex I apply from 2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [LinkedIn commentary](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)).

### Related Provisions
The EU AI Act Service Desk's guidance on Article 111 ties obligations for operators of pre-existing high-risk systems to systems "placed on the market before 2 August 2026" (medium confidence) ([Article 111 guidance](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)). However, the consolidated official EUR-Lex text (version dated 27.07.2026, reflecting the Omnibus amendment) instead references "the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113," suggesting the operative date for this provision has itself shifted in line with the new Annex III timeline (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Several sources still cite 2 August 2026 as the operative Annex III deadline, apparently predating or not accounting for the Omnibus amendment (low confidence, flagged) ([CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20), [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act), [RAIL](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)). One low-confidence news blog claims a further delay to 2 August 2029, which is unverified and conflicts with official sources confirming 2 December 2027 (low confidence, flagged) ([news blog](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update)). Another source states the Annex I transition runs to 2 August 2027 rather than 2028 (low confidence, flagged) ([Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)). A commentary describing these dates as negotiated "backstop dates" is also low confidence ([LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)), as is the attribution of the amendment to "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744" (low confidence) ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)).

## Knowledge Gaps
The precise statutory text and article number establishing the 2 December 2027 date is not fully quoted in available sources. The official citation for the Omnibus amending regulation remains unconfirmed by primary EU sources. It is unclear whether the 2029 delay claim reflects an actual further legislative step or inaccurate reporting. The interaction between Article 111(2)'s "significant changes" trigger and the new Annex III date is not fully resolved, nor is readiness of conformity assessment infrastructure (notified bodies, harmonised standards) for the 2027 deadline.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI System Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
As originally adopted, the EU AI Act set 2 August 2026 as the date on which obligations for high-risk AI systems under Annex III would apply (high confidence). However, following the "AI Omnibus"/Digital Omnibus simplification process, which entered into force on 27 July 2026, this deadline was postponed to **2 December 2027** for Annex III systems, with a separate date of **2 August 2028** for high-risk systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I (high confidence). Some commentary and news sources have not yet updated to reflect this change, and one unverified blog claims a further delay to 2029, creating notable confusion in the current source landscape.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (as adopted in 2024)
Under the AI Act as originally adopted, high-risk AI system obligations—including those under Annex III—were scheduled to become applicable 36 months after entry into force, on 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)).

### The Omnibus Amendment Process
The European Commission proposed adjusting the high-risk rules timeline by up to 16 months, so that obligations would begin only once the Commission confirmed that necessary standards and compliance tools were available (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). The "Digital Package on Simplification" (AI Omnibus) was formally adopted on 19 November 2025, political agreement between Council and Parliament was reached on 7 May 2026, and the amending regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) ([Shaping Europe's Digital Future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

### Current (Amended) Deadlines
As amended, obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in **Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027** (high confidence), corroborated by multiple EU guidance pages and legal-analysis sources ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [AI Omnibus Enters Into Force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force), [Timeline for Implementation](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)). Legal analysis of Article 113 confirms that Chapter III, Sections 1–3 (except Article 6(5)) apply from this date (medium confidence) ([Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). Separately, obligations for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products under **Annex I apply from 2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [LinkedIn commentary](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)).

### Related Provisions
The EU AI Act Service Desk's guidance on Article 111 ties obligations for operators of pre-existing high-risk systems to systems "placed on the market before 2 August 2026" (medium confidence) ([Article 111 guidance](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)). However, the consolidated official EUR-Lex text (version dated 27.07.2026, reflecting the Omnibus amendment) instead references "the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113," suggesting the operative date for this provision has itself shifted in line with the new Annex III timeline (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Several sources still cite 2 August 2026 as the operative Annex III deadline, apparently predating or not accounting for the Omnibus amendment ([CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20), [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)). One low-confidence news blog claims a further delay to 2 August 2029, which is unverified and conflicts with official sources confirming 2 December 2027 (low confidence, flagged) ([news blog](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update)). Another source states the Annex I transition runs to 2 August 2027 rather than 2028 (low confidence, flagged) ([Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)). A commentary describing these dates as negotiated "backstop dates" is also low confidence ([LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)), as is the attribution of the amendment to "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744" (low confidence) ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)).

## Knowledge Gaps
The precise statutory text and article number establishing the 2 December 2027 date is not fully quoted in available sources. The official citation for the Omnibus amending regulation remains unconfirmed by primary EU sources. It is unclear whether the 2029 delay claim reflects an actual further legislative step or inaccurate reporting. The interaction between Article 111(2)'s "significant changes" trigger and the new Annex III date is not fully resolved, nor is readiness of conformity assessment infrastructure (notified bodies, harmonised standards) for the 2027 deadline.
